gloss: to feel unwell; to be in bad condition; inconvenient

definitions.gloss: to feel unwell; to feel sick
definitions.explanation: Describes a person who is not feeling well physically. A common, polite way to express illness.

definitions.gloss: to be in bad condition; to not work properly
definitions.explanation: Describes a machine, device, or situation that is not functioning correctly.
Describes a situation that is troublesome or difficult to deal with.

notes:
⟦{具合|ぐあい}→具合：01391_guai⟧ means 'condition' or 'state,' so {具合|ぐあい}が{悪|わる}い literally means 'the condition is bad.' Its most common use is to describe feeling physically unwell — it is the standard, polite way to say you're sick in Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{体|からだ}→体：00784_karada⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{具合|ぐあい}が{悪|わる}い: to be in poor physical condition
- ⟦{胃|い}→胃：01706_i⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{具合|ぐあい}が{悪|わる}い: to have a bad stomach
- {具合|ぐあい}が{悪|わる}く⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to start feeling unwell; to malfunction
- {具合|ぐあい}が{悪|わる}そう: to look unwell

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{気分|きぶん}が{悪|わる}い→気分が悪い：24922_kibungawarui⟧: to feel sick; to feel bad — overlaps with sense 1 but can also mean emotionally bad or offended
- ⟦{調子|ちょうし}→調子：03491_choushi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{悪|わる}い→悪い：00908_warui⟧: to be out of form; in bad condition — similar across all senses but more informal
- ⟦{都合|つごう}が{悪|わる}い→都合が悪い：22996_tsugougawarui⟧: inconvenient — specifically about scheduling or circumstances, narrower than sense 3
